segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Pippa.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: And I'm Phil. What was your favourite game when you were a child, Pippa?

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: I think my favourite game was skipping with a skipping rope. How about you?

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Well, I could never skip, so I think I just prefer playing football.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Ah, well that's a good game to play in the playground.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: 80 years ago, it was quite common for children in Britain's cities to play in bomb sites,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: the ruins of houses which had been destroyed in World War II.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Today, the idea is back in fashion, with kids playing not in bomb sites,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: but in junk playgrounds, also called adventure playgrounds.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: In contrast to pre-made playgrounds, where swings and slides are fixed in place,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: adventure playgrounds provide pieces of building materials for kids to build things themselves.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Reporter William Cramer went to see one such playground in Wrexham,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: North Wales, for BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: At first glance, the land is little more than a junkyard.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: There are stacks of used wooden pallets and big reels for holding wires.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: But if you look a little bit closer, you'll see crooked homemade structures,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: hidey holes and turrets.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Children run barefoot. They swing on ropes and throw themselves down a makeshift waterslide.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: At first glance William sees only junk The phrase at first glance means looking at something for the first time before having a chance to look more carefully

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Adventure playgrounds are indeed full of junk pieces of

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: construction material like old tyres, planks of wood and lengths of rope. But look closely and

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: you'll see children using the junk to play, building dens and hidey holes. A hidey hole is a small

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: place for hiding things, or in this case, for children to hide themselves.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: In this episode, we'll be hearing how adventure playgrounds are giving kids the freedom and

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: space to play. As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases. And remember,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: you can find all this episode's vocabulary along with a transcript on our website,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: But now I have a question for you, Pippa. We know that adventure playgrounds started

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: of after the Second World War. But in which country? Was it A. France, B. Germany or C. Denmark?

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Hmm, I think maybe France. I think French children maybe were very adventurous.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: OK, well we'll find out the answer to that question later in the programme.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Adventure playgrounds give kids the freedom to choose how they play. According to child

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: development expert Dr Anna Housley-Justa, this freedom is vital as she explains here to BBC

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: World Service's People Fixing the World.

segments.speaker: Anna Housley Juster
segments.text: It's true. We do tend to minimise play in certain ways

segments.speaker: Anna Housley Juster
segments.text: but actually after the most basic needs are met for children so food shelter water safe place to be play is by far the most important factor for healthy child development

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Anna thinks play is as important as a child basic needs like food

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: and safety, but unfortunately the importance of play tends to be minimised. If something tends to

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: happen, it happens often and is likely to happen again.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Anna says that after a child's basic needs

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Demet, play is by far the most important factor in a healthy childhood. She uses the phrase

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: by far to mean by a great amount. For example, your teacher might say you're by far the best

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: student in class.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: The freedom to take controlled risks in a safe environment is what Anna calls

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: self-directed play. Here she explains more to Myra Anubi, presenter of BBC programme

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: people fixing the world. So what you're saying is letting kids play free play actually or play

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: on their own and kind of come up with the ideas that's really crucial for their development.

segments.speaker: Anna Housley Juster
segments.text: It's 100% crucial for their development in what I meant when I said that it's protective

segments.speaker: Anna Housley Juster
segments.text: is that kids build resiliency, confidence, coping strategies, regulation strategies. So many of the

segments.speaker: Anna Housley Juster
segments.text: skills that we know lead to healthy human development are developed in play.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Myra mentions the importance of free play and Anna says it's 100% crucial, meaning

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: completely You can also say 100 as an informal response to mean yes I agree with you completely

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Adventure playgrounds have lots of small dangers Hard pieces of wood sharp metal nails According to Anna taking small risks when playing with these

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: makes kids more resilient and builds coping strategies.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: A term for the psychological ways children develop

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: to manage challenging situations.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: And Phil, I think it's time for the answer to your quiz question.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Yes, I asked you in which country adventure playgrounds started.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: You said France, but I'm afraid the correct answer was Denmark.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: They were introduced by Danish architect Carl Theodor Sorensen.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learnt,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: starting with the phrase at first glance,

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: where you see something quickly without a chance to consider it more carefully.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: A hidey hole is a small place for hiding things in, or hiding yourself in.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: If people tend to do something, they do it often

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: and will probably continue to do it in the future.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: The phrase by far means by a great amount.

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: Saying 100% means completely

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: and can be used to emphasise a statement

segments.speaker: Phil
segments.text: or show that you totally agree with it.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: And finally, coping strategies are psychological ways

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: of managing your emotions in challenging situations.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Once again, our six minutes are up.

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: But remember, you can find many more trending topics

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: plus a quiz and worksheet for this episode on our website,

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: Hope to see you there soon

segments.speaker: Pippa
segments.text: but for now it's goodbye

segments.speaker: Phil
